articles.title: Putellas provides mindset change as London City bid to upstage champions
articles.summary: Ballon d’Or winner’s move to WSL has transformed the Lionesses on and off the pitch with belief soaring ahead of Manchester City clash. As Martin Semmens, the London City Lionesses chief executive, sits down is his office he looks like the cat that got the cream.
body: From the outside, it can feel slightly surreal. The independent women’s club, owned by the businesswoman Michele Kang, are third in the top flight, two and a half years after finishing eighth in tier two, and Semmens believes signing the world’s best player has helped changed everybody at the club’s mindset.

“Her impact on our commercial business is extraordinary,” he says. “From a leadership point of view, she allows us to start thinking about really winning. The environment today feels like it can beat Man City on Sunday and that’s a lot down to her.”

He acknowledges that Putellas, a World Cup winner with Spain and four-time European champion with Barcelona, and her brand – she has more Instagram followers (3.7m) than a men’s club the size of Porto, for example – were pivotal in helping the club secure what they claim is the largest front-of-shirt sponsorship deal in the women’s game, with Nike. The club say it is worth more than the new NWSL franchise Atlanta’s sponsorship of $4m (£3m) a year.

articles.title: ‘We are not in Disneyland’: Arteta warns Dowman of Arsenal’s demands
articles.summary: ‘We have made these mistakes … you can get punished’ Dowman lost appeal against red card at Fleetwood. Mikel Arteta has warned Max Dowman that he “is not in Disneyland” and must learn from his red card against Fleetwood after Arsenal’s appeal against his three-match suspension was rejected.
body: The 16-year-old became the youngest player ever to be sent off in League Cup history on Tuesday as the Premier League champions crashed out to League Two side Fleetwood. Arteta said he was “very disappointed” that the Football Association rejected their appeal against his red card and felt Dowman was lucky not to suffer a broken foot from “reckless tackles”.

But despite describing his reaction as “minimal”, the Arsenal manager revealed he had spoken to Dowman this week to underline his responsibilities after he was also sent off earlier this month playing for England’s Under 19s.

“I’ve done it, so I try to prevent that [in future]. That’s why I’m so protective of these things and especially with young players, because we have made those mistakes. You know how much you can get punished and how much it can change what happens next, and it’s not the first time, so obviously we need to put an end to it very, very quickly,” Arteta said.

articles.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream while Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
articles.summary: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United.
body: I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json.

As a Spurs supporter who saw my first game at White Hart Lane when I was five years old – almost eight decades ago – I can only express my relief that attention has drifted away from the continual ridicule of my team. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. It’s time for my second nap of the day now, so I’ll sign off” – Stewart McGuinness.

articles.title: South Africa-Australia set for classic finale – what does history suggest could happen?
articles.summary: South Africa set up an epic final day of their decisive Test against Australia by batting throughout the fourth day. What does history suggest could happen?
body: Having effectively began day four on 40-4, South Africa batted on and on against Australia in Cape Town to move from a position where defeat looked likely to one where a series victory is a real possibility.
In being bowled out for 387 in the final over - with Ryan Rickelton making 101 and Wiaan Mulder last man out for a brilliant 115 - South Africa set the tourists a target of 288 for victory.
WinViz - the tool analysts CricViz use to predict such results - gives the hosts a 54% chance of victory.
Australia's target is such that should they chase it on day five, it would be the second-highest fourth-innings chase in the 62 previous Tests on this famous ground.

articles.title: Moondra's record 6-26 helps Ireland force decider
articles.summary: Seamer Jai Moondra finishes with the best ever figures for an Ireland bowler in one-day international cricket as the tourists level their five-game series against Namibia with a comprehensive 130-run victory.
body: His 6-26 in Windhoek eclipsed Josh Little's 6-36 against Zimbabwe in 2023, the previous best for Ireland in the format.

With leading all-rounder Mark Adair still to feature in the series despite his place in the touring squad, Ireland's bowlers had allowed their hosts to top 300 twice in the first three games of the series, dropping both to trail 2-1.

But, after Tim Tector marked his ODI debut with a fine knock of 73 off 81 balls to set Namibia a target of 299, this time Moondra put his side in a commanding position with three early wickets to leave the hosts faltering at 32-3.

While a 57-run partnership for the eighth wicket between Zane Green and Ruben Trumpelmann offered brief resistance, Moondra accounted for both in the space of nine deliveries to claim his first international five-wicket haul.

articles.title: Wilkin: Rugby League World Cup format 'fundamentally flawed'
articles.summary: Sky Sports' Jon Wilkin believes the Rugby League World Cup format is "fundamentally flawed" after England were left on the brink of their first group-stage exit in the tournament's history.
body: England sealed a 34-12 victory against Papua New Guinea on Friday but needed to win by a margin of 68 points to give themselves a chance of leapfrogging Samoa in Pool B and C and advancing to the semi-finals on points difference.
Now their hopes rest on Tonga, who face off against Samoa on Sunday. England need Tonga to win by more than 46 points to secure a spot in the knockout stages.
The new tournament structure, which has been downsized from 16 teams to 10, came after Australia stepped in as hosts following France's withdrawal in 2023 for financial reasons.
It has effectively meant that each group game in Pool B and C has carried more jeopardy than before.

articles.title: How Suzuki has wowed Villa fans since replacing Martinez
articles.summary: Aston Villa fans still sing about having the world's number one goalkeeper. But what started as a chant for Emiliano Martinez and morphed into defiant support for young Japanese goalkeeper Zion Suzuki has become something else. They actually believe it.
body: Suzuki has been superb since joining from Parma in the summer. Not only has Martinez not been as missed as many anticipated, there is growing optimism that in his 24-year-old replacement, Villa have a goalkeeper who has even more facets to his game.

There have been some standout displays already. Suzuki was excellent in the win over Manchester City last time out, ending their 100-per-cent Premier League record under Enzo Maresca. The contrast with Gianluigi Donnarumma at the other end was stark.

While the Champions League winner allowed Nicolas Jackson's decider to go through him, Suzuki pulled off a series of stops, relieved pressure with his claims and looked far more composed with the ball at his feet. Only one of the two looked world class.

Suzuki had been identified by Paris Saint-Germain as a potential long-term replacement for Donnarumma, who left last year. But mooted plans to loan him out to continue his development helped convince the player that the plans at Villa were preferable.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli Dealing with ‘Viral Illness’ Ahead of Potential Formula 1 Championship-Clinching Race
articles.summary: NEED TO KNOW. Kimi Antonelli has a “viral illness,” his team said Thursday. Mercedes said the FIA excused the 20-year-old from Thursday media duties so he could rest. Antonelli could clinch the Formula 1 championship this weekend, which would make him F1’s youngest champion and Italy’s first in…
body: The 20-year-old Italian driver opted out of media obligations at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez on Thursday, Oct. 29, due to a “viral illness” ahead of the 2026 Mexico Grand Prix this weekend, Mercedes, his racing team, said.

“Kimi is feeling under the weather today as he recovers from a viral illness,” Mercedes said in a statement. “As a precaution, the FIA has excused him from his mandatory media duties to give him the chance to rest ahead of the weekend. We expect him to be back tomorrow.”

Rest and recovery are essential for Antonelli, who is on track to become the youngest Formula 1 champion of all time and the first Italian champion in over 70 years with a win at the Mexico Grand Prix. The Mercedes star is poised to beat Sebastian Vettel’s long-standing record for the youngest-ever champion (he was 23 years and 134 days old when he won his first title in 2010).

Antonelli is coming into the Mexico GP with a 123-point lead over teammate George Russell and 124 points over Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari. The Italian athlete only needs to get two points to secure the championship.

articles.title: Hollie Doyle glad to be back in the saddle
articles.summary: Sky Sports Racing’s ambassador Hollie Doyle prepares for her first rides back at Southwell on Saturday and previews the key contests from Keeneland at the Breeders' Cup on Saturday.
body: Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle is set to make her return to the saddle on Saturday with a nice book of rides at Southwell; Speaking to Simon Mapletoft, Hollie took time to preview her rides and take a look at the best of the action from the Breeders' Cup.

It's been a long, difficult road, but I'm finally back in the saddle at Southwell on Saturday, five months after breaking my left leg in a horrible fall at Bath. I comfortably passed my mandatory 'return to riding' test in midweek which clears me to take eight rides on the All-Weather.

There are so many people to thank for helping my recovery, in particular the Injured Jockeys Fund. Rob Treviss and Joe Baker at Oaksey House in Lambourn and my physiotherapist Daloni Lucas have all been amazing.

I've been working with those guys five days a week since I left hospital a few weeks after my fall and, in my mind, always aimed for an early November comeback, so I'm delighted to be on track and feeling good.

articles.title: Kerby Joseph misses Lions practice to close week
articles.summary: ALLEN PARK — The Detroit Lions still haven't taken the training wheels off Kerby Joseph, but according to coach Dan Campbell, it's been so far, so good, despite the All-Pro safety missing practice Friday, Oct. 30. "He's done a good job, and it's good so far," Campbell said.
body: "We still do some rehabilitation, get him some of those miles that he's not getting right now that he normally gets, the running, the volume."

The Lions opened Joseph's 21-day acclimation window on Wednesday, meaning they have three weeks to decide whether Joseph is healthy enough to be added back to the active roster or should be shut down for the remainder of the 2026 season because of a lingering knee injury. Campbell said the plan is to "have him in a real practice" next week.
Given how Campbell talked about his progress, Joseph's absence at Friday's practice was a surprise. But on the positive side: every player from the Lions' active roster was in attendance.
Joseph was wearing a compression sleeve on his leg on Thursday that he didn't have on Wednesday, which Campbell said isn't a big deal.

articles.title: PSG look to extend Quentin Ndjantou’s contract
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain are looking to extend Quentin Ndjantou’s (19) contract, as per a report from RMC Sport. The France youth international has made just one appearance for his formative club so far this season.
body: Ndjantou made his breakthrough into the first team last season, however, he has yet to build on that. He has been on the fringes of the set-up this season, playing just nine minutes across all competitions. Those minutes came off the bench in Ligue 1.

It is thought that, in the short term, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s ACL injury will provide Ndjantou with more opportunities to impress Luis Enrique. And PSG are also looking to the future with the left winger. As per RMC Sport, the reigning European champions are looking to tie him to a new five-year deal. Talks are already underway.
PSG are also looking to sign David Boly (17) to a first professional deal, the publication adds.
